finding: Two contradictory revenue datasets coexist in NBS FINAL delivery/04_Datasets
detail: Gross_Export_Revenue.csv (5 quarters, 128 artists, fixed 70% split, Flavour duplicated) vs Revenue_By_Platform_Quarterly.csv (31 quarters, 734 artists, observed split). Same quarters diverge 19.9%-36.4%.
evidence: _audit/ledger.md; ls -la of 04_Datasets shows 7 files dated Aug 11 vs 21 dated Aug 16-17
suspected_cause: NBS FINAL delivery was created as a copy of delivery/; 7 files were never regenerated by any pipeline stage and no script writes them
proposed_fix: Regenerate or remove the orphans; if removed, record in limitations that the Chartmetric-era figures remain available in delivery/ as immutable evidence

finding: Hosted site serves data predating every correction in this work

suspected_cause: Deployment built from commit c8fef8f; 123 files uncommitted locally
proposed_fix: Gate 2: commit, push, redeploy, then re-verify hosted values against source

finding: SPA rewrite masks missing API artifacts as HTTP 200 HTML
detail: vercel.json rewrites /(.*) to /index.html, so /api/v1/console/THIS-DOES-NOT-EXIST.json returns HTTP 200 with content-type text/html. A missing or mistyped data artifact is indistinguishable from a present one at the HTTP layer.
evidence: curl -o /dev/null -w %{http_code} on a nonexistent artifact returns 200; content-type text/html
suspected_cause: Catch-all rewrite has no exclusion for /api/
proposed_fix: Exclude /api/ from the SPA rewrite so missing artifacts return a real 404

finding: Uplift rate 0.40 contradicts the 0.30 used by the delivered file and the documented methodology
detail: backend/scripts/build_nbs_accounts.py:64 sets UNMEASURED_UPLIFT_RATE=0.40. The delivered Gross_Streaming_Revenue.csv reproduces at EXACTLY 0.30 (638/638 rows, $0.00 residual) and fails at 0.40 (634/638 rows, $5,809,678 residual). MethodologyInspector.tsx:351,356 documents 0.30. nbs_extract_new_artists.py:191 uses 0.30. Only nbs_deliverables.py:186 uses 0.40, and that script did not produce the delivered file. This inflates the 5 overlap quarters by $5,809,677.
suspected_cause: I adopted 0.40 from nbs_deliverables.py without checking it against the file actually delivered
proposed_fix: Change UNMEASURED_UPLIFT_RATE to 0.30 and regenerate all downstream artifacts

finding: Precedence keeps a Chartmetric value that is wrong by five orders of magnitude for Burna Boy
detail: Burna Boy Spotify monthly listeners: Chartmetric 160-184, Soundcharts 21,923,917 for the same dates (raw shard and live API agree exactly). The merge rule 'Chartmetric wins' keeps 167 and discards 21.9M - a factor of 128,964. Scope check across 128 artists with both providers: 125 agree within 2x, 1 is 6x (Lagbaja), 1 has Chartmetric higher, 1 is catastrophic (Burna Boy). Not systemic, but it affects Nigeria's largest export artist in every quarter from 2024.
suspected_cause: Chartmetric field appears to be in different units or corrupt for this artist; precedence applied blindly with no plausibility check
proposed_fix: Add a plausibility guard to the merge: where providers disagree by more than an order of magnitude, flag rather than silently prefer. Decision on which value to keep is NBS's.

finding: Observed split is aggregated portfolio-wide then applied uniformly to every artist
detail: One quarterly ratio (sum of Nigerian listeners / sum of total listeners) is computed and applied to every artist's revenue. Per-artist geography EXISTS in Geography_Full_Daily.csv.gz but is not used. The ratio is AGG; its application to an individual artist is ASM. Evidence base is ~90% of artists in the overlap quarters (e.g. Q2_2025: 644 of 716 have a domestic observation).
suspected_cause: Aggregate ratio was simpler and matched the shape of the old fixed-share model
proposed_fix: Either compute per-artist splits from the geography already held, or relabel the artist-level figure as ASM in every artifact

finding: 426 of 638 rows in the old file use ESTIMATED YouTube views, not observed
detail: youtube_views_source column: 'estimated' 426 rows, 'actual' 212. The old file's YouTube revenue is therefore two-thirds estimated. The new file uses observed channel-view deltas throughout. This accounts for -$6,837,373 of the streaming base change.
suspected_cause: Chartmetric track-level views denied; old pipeline substituted subscribers x 15
proposed_fix: None needed in the new file; document that the old figure was largely estimated

finding: Stock treated as flow: YouTube_channel_views_daily aggregated with rule 'sum'
detail: The metric is a cumulative counter (the catalogue's own limitation text says 'use net_change between dates for period volume') but both catalogues declare aggregation_rule='sum'. The merge Aggregator therefore sums ~90 daily LEVELS per quarter. 8,012 cells affected in Quarterly_Aggregates_Full.csv, summed total 62,589,979,921,793 'views'. Reference: Davido Q2_2025 published 177,639,619,700 vs correct net change 125,410,400 - inflation 1,416x. Reaches workbook 10 Quarterly_Headline (Q2_2025 cell 4,695,210,238,738) and Artist_Quarterly. Revenue is NOT affected: build_nbs_accounts.py:167 takes the quarter delta, clamped >=0.
suspected_cause: aggregation_rule copied from the catalogue where the limitation note and the rule contradict each other; the old delivery emitted zeros for this variable so the defect never produced a visible number until the new pipeline populated it
proposed_fix: Change aggregation_rule to net_change for YouTube_channel_views_daily in both catalogues (rule-based; regenerates), regenerate merge->standardise->workbooks->console. Also emit negative-delta quarters as blank-not-zero in aggregates or clamp with the same rule as revenue.

finding: Row count published as an artist headcount: the console reported '131 artists' in 25 places when the master list holds 131 ROWS describing 130 distinct artists
detail: "Flavour" and "Flavour N'abania" are one artist carried twice in the population frame under Chartmetric ids 56982 and 372062. Both identities are status='verified' and both produce a revenue row in all five delivered quarters, so the FIRST submission double counted the artist: $3,417,762.76 of delivered revenue sits under the alias, and its flat cost model billed N=131 rather than 130. The pipeline already deduplicated this (build_nbs_accounts.py), so no canonical figure is wrong; the defect was confined to the published console, which asserted a row count under the word 'artists'. Two of the claims were runtime templates ('{stats.universe} artists') that a source grep could not see and were caught only by rendering the page.
suspected_cause: The alias map existed as a copy-pasted literal in two build scripts and was never exposed to the frontend, so the console had no way to know a row count and an artist count differed
proposed_fix: Derive both counts in nmas/cohort.py from the delivered file, mirror them into a generated frontend artifact, and state each figure under its own name: MASTER_LIST_ROWS (131), DISTINCT_ARTISTS (130), COST_MODEL_N (131, kept because it records what the shipped cost model actually billed). GAP-033 now names the duplicate and its provider ids. Guarded by a drift test with four arms, each proven to fail on a planted defect.
